SendMessageRequest.description:
Body of POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages. `conversation_id` is in
the path; types.ts carries it in the object too, so it is accepted and
ignored rather than rejected by `extra='forbid'`.

`text` is required but may be **empty**, and the distinction is load-bearing.
Summary is template-driven and ignores the question entirely
(`SummaryWorkflow.run` takes `question: str = ""` and never reads it), so
focus instructions are optional — which is what the composer's "(optional)"
placeholder already promises the attorney. A `min_length=1` here made every
summary sent with an empty box a 422 raised before the route body ran.

No default, though: a body that omits `text` altogether is a client that
forgot a field rather than an attorney who typed nothing, and it stays a
422 naming the field.

An empty question *is* meaningless in every other mode, so it is still
rejected — in `turns._stream_turn`, beside the FR-19 draft guard, because
only the route knows the resolved intent: `POST /api/summarize` carries
whatever `mode` the caller sent and the route is what makes it a summary.
SendMessageRequest.title: SendMessageRequest

info.description:
Legal Lens — grounded reading and drafting over an attorney's own documents.

Every output is traceable to a retrieved span, or the system declines. A refusal
is a `200` carrying a structured `refusal` object, not an error: "not answerable
from your documents" is a first-class success state (FR-14, TS-3).

The wire is **camelCase**, matching `frontend/src/api/types.ts`.
info.title: Legal Lens API

set with scores, and the versions that produced the answer.

⊕ Re-read one turn. The frontend uses this after a reconnect to find out
whether a stream it lost actually completed — otherwise an interrupted
stream and a completed-but-unseen one are indistinguishable.

rather than being summed client-side over a partial page.

delete.description:
FR-26 at workspace level. Documents are hard-deleted; conversations,
traces and usage go with them. `audit_log` is retained — a tombstone is the
only record that survives, which is what DR-4 requires and what makes the
open question in BRD §16 about audit retention worth asking.
